clue.text: Reckon one million is put into property

indicators.note: something put into another thing ends up sitting inside it, so the short pieces go inside the longer word

blocks.note: an estate is land or property someone owns
the Roman numeral for one
the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A buyer works out the figure after a million is invested in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: I and M go together inside EST-ATE to give ESTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to reckon a figure roughly, judging an amount without exact calculation.

clue.text: Loudly made asinine sounds to add a ribbon

indicators.note: loudly means said out loud, so we want a word that is heard the same as the phrase

blocks.note: a donkey's noise is a bray, so an ass that made its noise brayed

explanation.surface: A donkey hee-haws while someone ties a ribbon on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Asinine looks like it means silly, but here it simply means of a donkey (Latin asinus).
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to braid is to trim clothing with decorative woven tape or ribbon.

clue.text: Phones for jewellery

blocks.note: first meaning: calls someone on the telephone
second meaning: bands worn on the fingers

explanation.surface: Someone calls to order some jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Rings is a verb for making telephone calls and a plural noun for finger jewellery bands.

clue.text: Briny wine at quay

blocks.note: the briny is a jocular name for the salty sea
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Salty-tasting wine drunk down by the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal harbour town, where ships tie up at its quays, serves loosely as the quay itself.

clue.text: Ring AA Milne's bear up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the bear in A. A. Milne's children's stories

explanation.surface: A request to telephone Winnie-the-Pooh's creator about the bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a verb for phoning, but it is the definition as a noun: a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, such as a child's toy or a barrel band, so a ring shape.

clue.text: Left ear's broken by intense beam

indicators.note: something broken falls into pieces that can be put back in another order

blocks.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left
taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone's left ear is damaged by a powerful beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser produces a narrow, concentrated and very powerful ray of light.

clue.text: Scarcity can make result dull

indicators.note: what a word can make is something new built from it, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a lack is a shortage or scarcity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shortages lead to a disappointing outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacklustre means without shine or energy, so flat, uninspired and dull.

clue.text: Cold place for larynx, but not very old

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the letters for the following words are taken away

blocks.note: the voice box is the everyday name for the larynx
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A sore-throat remedy of keeping the larynx chilled, unless you are quite elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: VOICEBOX loses its V and O to leave ICEBOX.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a chilled cabinet for keeping food, so a cold storage spot or refrigerator.

clue.text: Pull a face, if keeping a nicer sort of old container

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters come out in a new order
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to gurn is to pull a grotesque face, a British word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces at the idea of being kept as a nicer kind of person.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters go into GURN after its G. Keats wrote a famous ode to one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grecian urn is an ancient Greek vase or vessel, so an old container in the most literal sense.

clue.text: Closing off sound from top of room

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the words are heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: closing something off tightly is sealing it

explanation.surface: Soundproofing a room from noise coming down through the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound looks like noise in the surface, but it is the signal to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceiling is the overhead interior surface covering a room, its upper limit.

clue.text: Assistant for each daily

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: An assistant is hired on a day-by-day basis for every job.
explanation.walkthrough: Daily looks like an adjective; here it is a noun, a newspaper published every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper that comes out each weekday, and a paper is short for newspaper.

clue.text: Metal restraint

blocks.note: first meaning: the heavy soft grey element
second meaning: a strap for walking a dog

explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a heavy chemical element and also the British word for a dog's leash.

clue.text: Impecunious, in part due to this? (inits)

definitions.text: Impecunious, in part due to this?

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the word before it is used, a run of its letters

blocks.note: the run of letters sits inside this word

explanation.surface: Someone is broke, perhaps partly because of what they owe.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: running up promissory notes can leave you impecunious, meaning penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: An IOU is a written promise to pay a debt, and debts are a reason someone may be short of money.

clue.text: Hot and humid weather finally in issue

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word just before it
in places that letter inside the word that follows

blocks.note: an issue under discussion is a topic
the final letter of weather

explanation.surface: Muggy conditions eventually become the main talking point.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropic as an adjective means tropical, describing the hot humid climate near the equator.

clue.text: Small bird of some aptitude

indicators.note: of some means the answer is taken from some part of the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A little bird shows a certain talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tits are small songbirds such as the blue tit and great tit, common in British gardens.

clue.text: Pat clean displaced organ

indicators.note: displaced means moved out of position, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Pat cleans up after an organ is moved, like a surgical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The placenta is a temporary organ in the womb that nourishes the developing foetus.

clue.text: Quietly I get into bed, or into trouble

definitions.note: the clue's earlier 'get into' is shared: the sense is get into trouble

indicators.note: to get into a bed is to be inside it, so the first pieces go inside

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sneaky person creeps into bed quietly, or else ends up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Cop it is British slang for getting punished or getting into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop it is informal British slang meaning to be punished or be in serious bother.

clue.text: Permission for prisoner to be dispatched

blocks.note: a con is a convict
dispatched means sent off

explanation.surface: Authorisation is sought to transfer an inmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Consent is agreement or approval given to allow something, the same as permission.

clue.text: Understand why pronoun is so long

blocks.note: to see a point is to understand it
a second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a pronoun should be so lengthy.
explanation.walkthrough: So long looks like a comment on length, but it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: So long and see you are both casual farewells said when parting from someone.

clue.text: Two aides for dad

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant, or aide
the second of the two assistants

explanation.surface: A father gets a pair of helpers.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa is an old-fashioned or childish word for father, just like dad.

clue.text: Chrome without metal lid turns yellowy

indicators.note: a lid sits on top, so in a down answer it is the first letter of the word
without means lacking, so that letter is taken out
something that turns changes its position, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of metal

explanation.surface: A chrome fitting with its metal cap missing starts to discolour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment and the brownish-yellow colour named after it.

clue.text: Bad service causes offence

blocks.note: first meaning: a tennis serve that lands out
second meaning: a misdeed or error someone is to blame for

explanation.surface: Poor treatment in a shop or restaurant upsets a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: Service looks like the shop sort, but it is the tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a fault is an illegal serve; generally a fault is a misdeed or transgression.

clue.text: Periods of inactivity bars?

blocks.note: first meaning: breaks from activity
second meaning: supports something sits or leans on, as in arm or foot props

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that bars is not the pub or the prison sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Rests are breaks for relaxing, and also props or supports like a bar a cue or foot sits on.

clue.text: In-house, a rival brand

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A company's own product competes with a competitor's label.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand looks like a product name, but here it is the verb: mark by burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To sear is to scorch with a hot iron, exactly what branding livestock does.

clue.text: Detest a copper cover for foreign castle

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so the outer piece goes round the rest

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to detest is to hate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hates the police guard posted at a castle abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a police officer, but it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Chateau is French for castle, and also a grand country house in France.

clue.text: Bearing heavenly food, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: manna is the food sent from heaven in Exodus

explanation.surface: Someone carrying food from heaven, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike in a non-rhotic British accent, where the final R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing and manner both mean the way a person carries and conducts themselves.

clue.text: It was the talk of Rome

definitions.text: It was the talk of Rome

blocks.clueFragment: It was the talk of Rome
blocks.note: surface reading: some gossip everyone in the city discussed
setter's reading: the speech, the language, the ancient Romans spoke

explanation.walkthrough: The talk of the town is gossip; here talk means the tongue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin was the language of ancient Rome, so literally the talk spoken by its people.
